covering.note: Short spines poke out through its coarse brown fur.

size.note: It weighs 5 to 16 kg, the biggest of all echidnas.

diet.note: It mostly eats earthworms, plus insect grubs.

birth.note: It is a mammal that lays eggs.

young.note: A female lays a single egg every 2 or 3 years.

lifespan.note: One at Taronga Zoo in Sydney was nearly 60 years old in 2024.

clues.text: Its long snout curves down like a beak.
It has no teeth. It mashes food against hard ridges in its mouth.
Its long, sticky tongue is covered in tiny spines for catching worms.
When threatened, it curls into a spiny ball or quickly digs itself into the ground.
It has poor eyesight, and it hunts by smell.
It pokes its snout into soft soil and sniffs out worms, and it can even sense their tiny electric signals.
Its egg hatches in a pouch on the mother's belly, and the baby, called a puggle, grows there.
It lives in rainforests on steep, rugged mountains, even in rocky limestone country.
Hunters use trained dogs that can follow its scent to where it sleeps during the day.

facts.text: It is one of only five kinds of mammal alive today that lay eggs: the platypus and four echidnas.
A skin in a museum, collected in 1901, shows it once lived in the Kimberley region of Australia too.
Its body stays cooler than most mammals', between 28 and 35 °C.
It has no outer ears, just slits behind its eyes.
A newly hatched puggle weighs just 1 or 2 grams, and has no hair or spines yet.
Its numbers are thought to have dropped by 80% in about 45 years, mostly from hunting.
